games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: What does 'coal' mean?
choices: A small soft bag that holds little things
A hard black rock that people burn for heat and energy
Areas or parts of a country that share something in common together
A problem that people discuss and try to solve
rounds.answer: A hard black rock that people burn for heat and energy
rounds.explanation: Coal is a black rock we burn to make heat and electricity.

rounds.prompt: What does 'pouch' mean?
choices: A very large area of land that is ruled by one single government
A written rule that guides a group's choices
A restless mood when people feel unhappy
A small soft bag or pocket used to hold little things
rounds.answer: A small soft bag or pocket used to hold little things
rounds.explanation: A pouch is a small bag; the family carried a paper inside a worn pouch.

rounds.prompt: What does 'independence' mean?
choices: To share information or ideas with other people
A group of words that someone has said or written
Being able to look after yourself and make your own choices
Surprising and sudden, because it was not planned or predicted at all
rounds.answer: Being able to look after yourself and make your own choices
rounds.explanation: Independence means making your own choices, as Amal did at the court.

rounds.prompt: What does 'issue' mean?
choices: A problem or topic that people discuss because it needs solving
A city or busy town rather than the countryside
The open countryside, with farms, wide fields and very few buildings around
Extremely angry, so calm is hard to keep
rounds.answer: A problem or topic that people discuss because it needs solving
rounds.explanation: The wasted plastic cups were an issue the students wanted to fix.

rounds.prompt: What does 'policy' mean?
choices: A young sheep, or the meat that comes from it
Feeling worried or nervous about something soon
The quiet countryside, with farms, open fields and very few buildings
A plan or rule that guides the choices a group makes
rounds.answer: A plan or rule that guides the choices a group makes
rounds.explanation: A policy is a guiding rule, like a school policy about spelling.

rounds.prompt: What does 'lobby' mean?
choices: Done too quickly, without thinking it through
A large open area inside a building where people wait
To make someone agree by giving good reasons
The ability to learn, to understand and to think about things carefully
rounds.answer: A large open area inside a building where people wait
rounds.explanation: The class met the curator in the museum lobby.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What does Amal understand about her role by the end of the passage?
choices: She understands that opening the courthouse doors each morning is important, because without her nothing there can begin.
The group leader's figures show hundreds of cups are used each week and none are recycled, so the waste is a real issue.
She says no, the storm was part of the journey, and it led to a well that had never been recorded before.
rounds.answer: She understands that opening the courthouse doors each morning is important, because without her nothing there can begin.
rounds.explanation: The passage ends with Amal seeing that she opens the court, so justice starts on time each day.

rounds.prompt: Which detail shows that Amal helps the visiting family straight away?
choices: He says he would rather research it first, because nobody should sign anything they have not read.
The author says Leo has honoured the old tradition of passing stories on by memory, and this time Leo feels pride instead of fear.
She does not hesitate; she leads the family inside and fills the water jug on the judge's bench.
rounds.answer: She does not hesitate; she leads the family inside and fills the water jug on the judge's bench.
rounds.explanation: The text says Amal did not hesitate and led the family in, showing she acts quickly and kindly.

rounds.prompt: What does Sami say before the friends agree to sign anything?
choices: The class turns it into a book that will be shared with next year's pupils.
He says he would rather research it first, because nobody should sign anything they have not read.
She says that a team which works well together is the most powerful kind of constitution.
rounds.answer: He says he would rather research it first, because nobody should sign anything they have not read.
rounds.explanation: Sami insists on reading and researching before signing, which shows careful, independent thinking.

rounds.prompt: What does the cracked charter come to mean to the class by the end?
choices: It becomes a lesson that even a crack, or fracture, can lead to a stronger foundation.
She says that a team which works well together is the most powerful kind of constitution.
Keeping her daily promise to unlock the court, and helping the anxious boy's family, help Amal see herself as a leader.
rounds.answer: It becomes a lesson that even a crack, or fracture, can lead to a stronger foundation.
rounds.explanation: The passage closes by saying the cracked charter now means that a fracture can build something stronger.

rounds.prompt: How does Amal answer the judge who asks whether the storm was a mistake?
choices: It becomes a lesson that even a crack, or fracture, can lead to a stronger foundation.
She understands that opening the courthouse doors each morning is important, because without her nothing there can begin.
She says no, the storm was part of the journey, and it led to a well that had never been recorded before.
rounds.answer: She says no, the storm was part of the journey, and it led to a well that had never been recorded before.
rounds.explanation: Amal tells the judge the storm was part of the journey and produced a valuable discovery.

rounds.prompt: What happens to the Memory Wall after it is taken down?
choices: She does not hesitate; she leads the family inside and fills the water jug on the judge's bench.
The class turns it into a book that will be shared with next year's pupils.
He admits he was too forceful, and that Amal's slower, more careful plan was wiser and led to a profitable find.
rounds.answer: The class turns it into a book that will be shared with next year's pupils.
rounds.explanation: The passage says the wall was not thrown away but made into a book for future pupils.
